legend: Ocular classification of naevus of Ota by Vishnevskia-Dai. The numbers represent the anatomical parts: surface-only involvement of the conjunctiva and/or sclera, iris, choroid, or iris and choroid. The letters represent the number of involved quadrants: A, one quadrant; B, two quadrants; C, three quadrants; D, four quadrants. If only the surface (conjunctiva and/or sclera) of the eye is involved, the eye will be classified as 1. Involvement of the surface with another part of the eye will be classified as the anatomical part involved and designated with “+” for the surface involvement: surface and iris (2+), surface and choroid (3+), or surface and iris and choroid (4+). No “+” will be added when no surface involvement is present.

legend: Left eye: Class 4D+ naevus of Ota showing loss of iris crypts and the presence of iris mammillations.
Bilateral hyperpigmentation. Conjunctival melanosis, scleral melanocytosis, and iris hyperpigmentation. Ocular class 4D+.
Ocular surface four-quadrant involvement (scleral melanocytosis and conjunctival melanosis) class 4D+.
Heavily pigmented spindled melanocytic cells of ocular melanocytosis in the choroid, sparing the choriocapillaris.
Heavily pigmented spindled melanocytic cells of ocular melanocytosis within the ciliary body.
